withdrawn_entry.latin_diff: none: the two texts are identical word for word and point for point.
withdrawn_entry.witness_note: The MR2002 text is not held here; this is the English of the antecedent oration roman-1962/most-holy-name-of-jesus/Collect, which the roman-1862 Pustet printing gives this day and whose Latin stands beside the formerly recorded postconciliar Latin in `latin_diff` above, mechanically diffed and not summarised. The 1962 row was read at printed p. 95 = leaf n105, collated page-image 2026-08-20; this proposal copies its translation rows BYTE-EXACT and adds no new reading. The 1861 keeps this feast on the SECOND SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY, not on 3 January: leaf n104, printed p. 94, heads it `II. SUNDAY after EPIPHANY. The FEAST of the HOLY NAME JESUS.` The postconciliar calendar keeps it on 3 January as an Optional memorial. The day is not the same day; the prayer is.

translations.text: O God, who didst appoint thy only begotten Son the Saviour of mankind, and commandest that his name should be called JESUS: mercifully grant, that we who venerate his holy name on earth, may also enjoy his sight in heaven. Thro'.

withdrawn_entry.antecedent_overlay: src/sources/inventories/roman-1962-proper-translations-v1.toml (mass most-holy-name-of-jesus, proper Secret; printed p. 96 = leaf n106, collated page-image 2026-08-20)
withdrawn_entry.latin_diff: none: the two texts are identical word for word and point for point.
withdrawn_entry.witness_note: The MR2002 text is not held here; this is the English of the antecedent oration roman-1962/most-holy-name-of-jesus/Secret, which the roman-1862 Pustet printing gives this day and whose Latin stands beside the formerly recorded postconciliar Latin in `latin_diff` above, mechanically diffed and not summarised. The 1962 row was read at printed p. 96 = leaf n106, collated page-image 2026-08-20; this proposal copies its translation rows BYTE-EXACT and adds no new reading. Same feast and same caution as the Collect above. The 1962 row records that the page sets no Latin cue before this Secret and sets a second `SECRET of the Sunday` after it; the text carried here is the first, the Mass's own.

translations.text: May thy blessing, O most merciful God, by which every creature is enlivened and subsists, sanctify this our sacrifice, which we offer thee in honour of the name of thy Son, our Lord Jesus Christ: that it may be acceptable to the praise of thy majesty, and available to our salvation. Thro' the same.

The 1962 row was read at printed pp. 96-97 = leaves n106-n107, collated page-image 2026-08-20; this proposal copies its translation rows BYTE-EXACT and adds no new reading. translations.text: O almighty and eternal God, who didst both create and redeem us, mercifully hear our prayers, and vouchsafe, with a pleasing and kind countenance, to receive the sacrifice of this victim of our salvation, which we have offered to thy divine majesty, in honor of the name of thy Son, our Lord Jesus Christ; that thy grace being poured on us, thro' the glorious name of Jesus, as a pledge of our eternal predestination, we may rejoice that our names are written in heaven. Thro' the same.

withdrawn_entry.verified_heading: I. SUNDAY AFTER EPIPHANY. (running head; see the Prayer over the Offerings above)
withdrawn_entry.verified_note: Read at 200 dpi on the page image; the page sets the cue `P. COMM. Praesta, quaesumus.` NOT THE 2002 PRAYER. The seasonal `epiphany` mass's `Mass during the Day` Prayer after Communion in this file reads `Caelesti lumine, quaesumus, Domine, semper et ubique nos praeveni`, which is a different oration; the reform changed this slot, and this English answers only the antecedent Latin the christological entry carries.
withdrawn_entry.witness_note: The MR2002 text is not held here; this is the English this 1861 printing made for the antecedent oration, read on its page by this lane and carried because the formerly recorded postconciliar Latin at this slot is that oration. Latin cue on the page: Praesta, quaesumus.. No 1962 overlay row answers this slot and none was reused: the roman-1962 index's entry for this day, `epiphania-domini`, records only its scripture-bearing propers and carries no oration at all, so the overlay has nothing filed against it. Nothing here is copied from another entry.

translations.text: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that our minds may be so purified, as to understand what we celebrate on this great solemnity. Thro'.

No English wording is retained.

method: Prep helper re-located and re-read every installed Latin and English word on fresh page-image crops (montages prep-p4/img/t<n>.png; specs prep-p4/mkcrops.py) and the target wording on the 2002 secondary PDF text layer cross-checked against rendered pages, or on OLM 1981 page images; word streams compared mechanically under orthographic folding (prep-p4/verify_b5.py).
